items.title: Continuous sample paths give continuous marginal laws

source.anchor: Original Samplinglib supplement. Pass almost-sure time convergence to weak convergence of the same pushforward laws.
source.attribution: Original Samplinglib supplement. The linked Mathlib source supplies the stated analytic background.

items.statement: Let \(\rho_t\) be the pushforward law of the random state at time \(t\). Almost-sure continuity of whole sample paths implies continuity of the map from time to marginal law in the topology of integration against bounded continuous tests.
assumptions: Time ranges over a first-countable topological space. The sample law \(P\) is a probability measure on a measurable space.
The state space is topological and measurable, with measurable open sets. Each time slice \(X_t\) is measurable.
There is a single full-measure event on which each time path is continuous on the entire time space.

formulae.label: Claim
formulae.tex: t\mapsto\rho_t,\qquad \rho_t=(X_t)_\#P,\qquad t\mapsto\int g\,d\rho_t\text{ is continuous for every bounded continuous }g.

obligations.label: Pass almost-sure time convergence to weak convergence of the same pushforward laws.

bindings.boundary: The conclusion is continuity in the weak topology of probability measures.

assumption_deltas.source: A single almost-sure event of continuous paths and measurable time slices.
assumption_deltas.lean: Every time slice is measurable and whole time paths are continuous almost surely.
assumption_deltas.reason: The same event supplies convergence for each fixed time.

items.title: Marginal balance from a centered sample increment

source.anchor: Original Samplinglib supplement. Apply signed Fubini to the centered increment and identify the actual marginals.
source.attribution: Original Samplinglib supplement. The linked Mathlib source supplies the stated analytic background.

items.statement: For each time \(v\), let \(\rho_v=(X_v)_\#P\). A sample increment equal almost surely to a signed time integral plus an integrable centered residual gives the following balance for the marginal expectations.
assumptions: The sample law \(P\) is a probability measure and the state space is measurable. Each slice \(X_v\) is measurable for every real \(v\).
The real test \(g\) is measurable. For each time \(v\), the state section \(A(v,\cdot)\) is measurable. The two random variables \(g(X_a)\) and \(g(X_b)\) are integrable.
The map \((v,\omega)\mapsto A(v,X_v(\omega))\) is integrable for the time-first product of Lebesgue measure restricted to \((\min(a,b),\max(a,b)]\) and \(P\).
The endpoints \(a,b\) are arbitrary reals. The signed integral identity \(g(X_b)-g(X_a)=\int_a^b A(v,X_v)\,dv+Z\) holds almost surely, where \(Z\) is integrable with expectation zero.
Product integrability gives integrable spatial drift sections for almost every restricted time. Spatial integrals use Lean's totalized Bochner convention at any exceptional time.

obligations.label: Apply signed Fubini to the centered increment and identify the actual marginals.

bindings.boundary: The sample increment identity and the centered residual are supplied.

assumption_deltas.source: Drift integrable on restricted time-first product and integrable centered residual.
assumption_deltas.lean: Integrable along the path for volume.restrict (uIoc a b) times P, with an integrable residual of expectation zero.
assumption_deltas.reason: The product gives integrability of the sample integral and Fubini for either endpoint order.

items.title: Differentiating a local marginal balance

source.anchor: Original Samplinglib supplement. Use the continuous averaged generator and differentiate the local integral identity.
source.attribution: Original Samplinglib supplement. The linked Mathlib source supplies the stated analytic background.

items.statement: For a weakly continuous curve of laws \(\rho_t\), set \(F(t)=\int g\,d\rho_t\) and \(B(t)=\int A(t,x)\,d\rho_t(x)\). A local signed balance about \(s\) gives the ordinary derivative of \(F\) at \(s\).
assumptions: The state space is compact and topological with measurable open sets. The curve \(t\mapsto\rho_t\) consists of probability laws, is defined for real times, and is weakly continuous.

The scalar field \(A\) is jointly continuous on real time times state. The function \(g\) is real-valued, and the statement uses Lean's totalized Bochner integral. The given balance uses those same integrals.
The signed balance holds for all \(u\) in a neighborhood of the real time \(s\).

obligations.label: Use the continuous averaged generator and differentiate the local integral identity.

bindings.boundary: This is the pointwise derivative under a jointly continuous field and a local balance on the real line.

assumption_deltas.source: Continuous field and law curve with local signed identity for the same integral.
assumption_deltas.lean: Joint continuity of A, weak continuity of the law and eventual equality in the real neighborhood filter.
assumption_deltas.reason: The real neighborhood supplies an ordinary two-sided derivative; both occurrences of the observable use Lean's Bochner convention.

items.title: Bounded measurable coefficients along progressive paths

source.anchor: Original Samplinglib supplement. Compose on filtration prefixes and use a uniform horizon bound for time sections and the sample-first product.
source.attribution: Original Samplinglib supplement. The linked Mathlib source supplies the stated analytic background.

items.statement: The scalar process \(b(t,\omega)=c(t,X_t(\omega))\) is strongly progressive. Its time section is integrable for every sample on the specified horizon and it has the indicated product-space \(L^p\) membership.
assumptions: The state space is pseudometrizable with its Borel measurable structure. The sample measure \(\mu\) is finite and its filtration is indexed by nonnegative time.

The process \(X\) is jointly measurable and strongly progressive. The real coefficient \(c\) on nonnegative time times state is Borel measurable. A finite constant bounds \(|c(t,w)|\) for all \(t\le T\) and all states \(w\).
The horizon \(T\) is nonnegative and \(p\) is any extended nonnegative real exponent.
The symbol \(\ell_T\) denotes Lebesgue time restricted to \([0,T]\).

obligations.label: Compose on filtration prefixes and use a uniform horizon bound for time sections and the sample-first product.

bindings.boundary: The coefficient bound is pointwise on the selected horizon, which yields time integrability at every sample.

assumption_deltas.source: Joint Borel coefficient with an absolute bound for all states and horizon times.
assumption_deltas.lean: Measurable c and an existential real bound pointwise for t ≤ T and every state.
assumption_deltas.reason: The same bound yields the time-section assertion for every sample and the sample-first product assertion for each extended exponent.

assumption_deltas.source: Joint measurability and strong progressiveness of the state process.
assumption_deltas.lean: Explicit joint product measurability and strong measurability on every filtration prefix.
assumption_deltas.reason: The two measurability interfaces supply time sections and filtration-relative composition.

items.title: From centered increments to a two-time marginal balance

source.anchor: Original Samplinglib supplement. Combine centered balance, a locally bounded primitive and Lebesgue differentiation.
source.attribution: Original Samplinglib supplement. The linked Mathlib source supplies the stated analytic background.

items.statement: Write \(\rho_t=(X_t)_\#P\). On the real time axis put \(F(t)=\int g\,d\rho_{t^+}\) and \(B(t)=\int A(t^+,w)\,d\rho_{t^+}(w)\), with \(t^+=\max(t,0)\). Then \(B\) is locally Lebesgue integrable, and \(F\) is absolutely continuous on every finite nonnegative interval and satisfies the displayed identities.
assumptions: The state space is compact and second countable with its Borel measurable structure. The sample measure \(P\) is a probability measure. The state process \(X\) is jointly measurable and the real test \(g\) is continuous.
The scalar field \(A\) is jointly measurable. For each \(T\ge0\) one finite constant bounds \(|A(t,w)|\) for every \(0\le t\le T\) and every state \(w\).

For each nonnegative \(t\), on a full-measure event for that time, \(g(X_t)-g(X_0)=\int_0^t A(v,X_v)\,dv+Z_t\), where \(Z_t\) is integrable and has expectation zero. Both endpoints \(a,b\) in the conclusion are arbitrary nonnegative times, with the signed integral convention.

obligations.label: Combine centered balance, a locally bounded primitive and Lebesgue differentiation.

bindings.boundary: The ordinary derivative assertion holds for Lebesgue-almost every strictly positive real time.

assumption_deltas.source: Centered pathwise balance for each nonnegative terminal time and a uniform bound on every finite horizon.
assumption_deltas.lean: For each horizon the centered residual and almost-sure identity are supplied; the bound holds at every state and horizon time.
assumption_deltas.reason: The uniform bound ensures integrability for Fubini and local Lipschitz control of the marginal expectation.

assumption_deltas.source: Actual time-slice laws, signed interval balance, local absolute continuity, and ordinary derivative almost everywhere on positive time.
assumption_deltas.lean: ProbabilityMeasure.map, nonnegative signed endpoints, absolute continuity on every finite nonnegative interval, and HasDerivAt for volume.restrict (Ioi 0) almost every t.
assumption_deltas.reason: The integral of the generator on the real axis uses its extension by nonnegative time, and the derivative is asserted on the positive half-line.
